## Natural history notes

A small fruticose lichen characterized by gray-green basal scales and slender upright peg-like stalks that often appear powdery or granular toward the tips. In Florida, it is found on sandy soil, humus, rotting wood, logs, and other acidic, nutrient-poor substrates in pinewoods, scrub, disturbed sandy areas, and open habitats with enough light and moisture. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, helping colonize exposed surfaces while absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air rather than feeding on plants or wood directly.
